claims.author_statement: Engine periodicity contributes spectral harmonics; tracked motion adds track/sprocket periodicity. Track contributions need not dominate airborne sound.
claims.interpretation: Mechanical plausibility for coarse cues does not establish model recognition.

claims.author_statement: Table 5 lists Leopard 1 and Leopard 2 as four-stroke V10 and V12 diesels. Dominant spectral lines are not necessarily firing-frequency peaks.
claims.interpretation: Do not infer cylinders, RPM or firing order from the largest peak alone.

claims.author_statement: Within each pass, two thirds trained and one third tested; acoustic-only full-pass recognition was 89%.
claims.interpretation: This split does not verify transfer to new independent sessions or physical vehicles.

claims.author_statement: Relative harmonic powers vary with rotation rate and observation angle.
claims.interpretation: Order normalization alone need not remove state or recording geometry.

claims.author_statement: The method chiefly recognizes engine/exhaust types; different vehicle types sharing engines can be grouped together.
claims.interpretation: A strong engine cue is not automatically a model identity cue.

claims.author_statement: The US ARL dataset uses five anonymized vehicle classes, two tracked and three wheeled.
claims.interpretation: Named model and variant identities remain unknown.

claims.author_statement: Each class has six runs; three runs train and three test. Harmonic features vary within classes and overlap across classes.
claims.interpretation: Run holdout offers more separation than within-pass splitting; session and individual identities remain unknown.

claims.author_statement: The other three runs test; SVM parameter selection uses training data only.
claims.interpretation: Adopt training-only preprocessing/selection; do not infer independent recording sessions from runs.
